title: Peddler’s Plan
text: A pet? Filo-tan is a pet…? Hmm, is that so? But Filo-tan as a pet…
“Yeah. I get the gist of it… so… actually, Motoyasu, if you’re stuck in a loop, you’ll remember this.”
“Remember what, exactly?”

“Back when I was summoned, I was just a normal guy, so I wouldn’t bring up such weird stuff. Even if I wanted to believe it, I’d be skeptical. Or rather, even if I thought it was true, my mind would automatically push it aside.”
“I see. Got it.”

So, my father just can’t bring himself to believe me because he’s worried about things like me sleeping with a man or something like that. …Come to think of it, it is a bit strange for a man’s father to be sleeping with a man. But for me, when it comes to Filolial-sama, gender doesn’t matter at all.
“At the very least, you should explain that you took in the girl you like as an adopted daughter. If you do that, I think he’ll probably accept it.”

That’s the advice my Father gave me. I see—if she’s an adopted daughter, even if she’s a girl, it shouldn’t be a problem. Filo-tan isn’t a pet, you know. I, Motoyasu, burned Father’s words deep into my brain.
“So? Why did you just stand by and watch me get trapped?”
“That’s what my future Father told me. He wanted me to act in a way that would make use of my knowledge of the future.”
“Hmm… Why did he say something like that?”
“It’s because when you went to Siltvelt, wars broke out with various countries, and it ceased to be a place where you fought the Waves.”
“Huh? But I was trying not to seek revenge, wasn’t I?”
“Yes. But—”

I explained to my future father the problems that occurred in the previous loop… the fox demon disguised as the Hero of the Takt and the Hero of the Claw, and the war between Shieldfreeden and Melromarc. Finally, I explained that it all ended with Itsuki being killed, which caused the loop to restart.
“If I go to Siltvelt, it’ll lead to a war on that massive a scale…”
My future father was speechless at the magnitude of the situation.
“Should I go? If that’s what you want, Father, I’ll go—this time for real.”
“It’s true that with Motoyasu-kun here, who knows how things will unfold later, we might be able to make things turn out better than before…”
My words caused Father’s expression to cloud over.

“No… I think Motoyasu-kun’s thinking is right. If the alternative is having all those problems happen, and all I have to do is hold out for three months, this option is more rewarding. As long as we don’t stir up any unnecessary trouble… After all, I wasn’t summoned to this other world to wage war.”
“Understood.”
“Working to prevent a war from breaking out. It really does feel like I’ve come from the future, doesn’t it?”
“That’s right. This Motoyasu will do anything for you, Father.”
“So? Motoyasu, you want to stay here in Melromarc with me to prevent the loop from happening again, right?”
“Yes, that’s right.”
My father sat down in a chair and stretched out his legs.
“So, in three months, that king and Myne are going to get a taste of their own medicine… I guess I’ll just have to wait and see.”
“Yes. I was told not to resort to force to resolve the situation.”
“Got it. Until then, I guess I just need to get stronger little by little.”
“You just need to get stronger while staying as inconspicuous as possible. Don’t worry—I’ll teach you how to do it.”
“Yeah, thanks. I’m counting on you.”
Just then, a crackling sound began coming from my pocket. I pulled an egg out of my pocket. It looked like Yuki-chan and Kou were about to hatch right then and there.
“Motoyasu-kun, did you buy a Filolial egg with your dowry money?”
“That’s right.”
Soon, with a soft cracking sound, Yuki-chan and Kou peeked their heads out of the egg.
“Peep!”
“Wow… they’re so cute.”
Yuki-chan and Kou emerged from the egg full of energy, hopping onto my hand, while my father peered down at them.
“So these are the monsters that grow up to pull carriages around town…”

My father watched them with a look of wonder. It can’t be helped—at this point, he doesn’t know much about Filolial-sama yet. Filolial-sama is a mysterious being. That’s precisely why I, Motoyasu, long for him so deeply.
“Have you decided on their names yet?”
“Yes, we have. My future Father named these little ones.”
“Really? What are their names?”
“Why don’t you try guessing? By the way, these two aren’t named Shiro-chan, Kiiro, or Chick. The white one is a female, and the yellow one is a male.”
“Hmm…”
My future father pondered as he watched Yuki-chan and Kou bouncing around energetically.
“This one’s white like snow, so Yuki-chan, and that one’s yellow, so Kou, maybe?”
“As expected of you, Father. You got it right.”
“Really? I struggled with it quite a bit, but I’m glad I got it right. I wonder if the loop has something to do with this kind of thing too…”
Yuki-chan and Kou bounced around energetically.
“Well then… I’d like you to register the one who served as your bodyguard in the future.”
I showed Father Sakura-chan’s unhatched egg.
“This is Sakura-chan. She’s a child whose monster crest hasn’t been registered yet.”
“Are you giving this to me?”
“Well, not exactly… but she was the one who served as your bodyguard, and she was very attached to you. I kept her around because I thought it would be best to let you be her master this time.”
“Ah, thank you…”
Father accepted Sakura-chan’s egg.
“Do you know how to register it?”
“Is it where you smear blood on the pattern painted on this egg?”
“That’s right. After that, just put it in an incubator, and Sakura-chan will hatch in a day.”
“Huh… Well, if I can’t find any other allies, maybe she’ll become a reliable companion?”
Father asked the old man at the weapon shop for a knife, lightly cut his finger, and completed the registration.
“So? What do we do now?”
“Well… my future Father, after this…”

That’s when I start thinking. Something’s off here. I can’t for the life of me remember what my Father was doing. I mean, I could guess that he’d bought my Big Sister and was slowly leveling her up, but what else was he doing?
“Motoyasu-kun?”
I do remember that he used to travel around as a peddler with his slave. As for the goods… I believe he was selling medicines of some sort.
“Before the loop, my Father used to earn money by peddling.”
“Peddling? Does that mean he traveled around to different places selling things?”
“That’s right. I remember him taking Filo-tan with him as he wandered from place to place selling goods. He’d often brush right past me when I was chasing pigs.”
I can still picture it now. Whenever Filo-tan saw my face, she’d let out a ferocious growl and kick me. That pain is the bond that ties Filo-tan and me together.
“You’re saying that with such a dreamy look on your face, but isn’t that a bit extreme? I mean, kicking you away…?”
“That was Filo-tan’s way of scolding me—and showing her love…”
“Hey, Motoyasu-kun? Come back here—”
“No good… He’s lost in his memories and won’t come back.”
Filo-tan. Where on earth have you gone? I’ll definitely pull fate in my direction and find you.
“A traveling merchant, huh… I’m not really sure what she was selling, but since she was fighting alone and penniless, she probably didn’t have much capital to begin with… How did she manage that?”
It seems Father is deep in thought.
“I’m pretty sure he was concocting potions!”
“Whoa! Don’t suddenly snap back to normal like that! You’ll give me a heart attack!”
My Father, looking startled, has Yuki-chan and the others perched on his shoulders.
“Concocting potions? Did I learn how to make potions?”
“There’s no doubt about it. Your future father made potions and sold them for money.”
“I’ve seen potion-making in games and stuff… but can you actually do it that well?”
“You can craft them using the Weapons skill. But the Father used to make them by hand, too.”
Come to think of it, the Father was quite the jack-of-all-trades. He had a talent for cooking, was well-liked by everyone, and even knew how to prescribe potions.

“Hmm… I see. If I can make them with the Shield skill, I’ll give it a try, but since I don’t know what kind of herbs I need, I’ll pop into the apothecary. I also don’t know what kind of shield requires the Alchemy skill.”

Come to think of it, unlike me, my Father’s shield gets reset. That means I’ll need to go defeat some monsters so he can learn the Alchemy skill. I’ll look in the Weapon Book for a spear with an alchemy recipe. …Ah, there it is. I remember where they live, too.
“Once I’ve geared up… I’ll learn the skill and start peddling… Yeah. I think I’ve got a plan for the time being.”
“All that’s left is to find a vendor to work with while I’m peddling.”
“Oh, right. People might not buy potions made by the Shield Hero, who’s our religious enemy. But then again, Motoyasu-kun…”
“What is it?”
My father is looking at me with a puzzled expression. Did I do something strange?

“Hmm… a problem has suddenly popped up. What should I do about the salespeople? It’d be a real pain if I got betrayed again… Hiring people from Siltvelt seems risky… but if I leave it to some random adventurer, they’ll probably embezzle the profits.”
He’s grumbling to himself.
“In cases like that, it’s best to use slaves!”
“Slaves!?”
